what_it_does: When chip designers finish routing wires and placing components, they run detailed electrical simulations (SPICE) to verify the design works. But modern advanced chips have billions or trillions of tiny parasitic effects (stray capacitances and resistances from wiring) that make simulation extremely slow. This work uses sensitivity analysis—a mathematical technique from calculus—to identify which parasitics actually matter for correctness and which are negligible. By keeping only the critical parasitics and removing the rest, simulation speed improves dramatically without sacrificing accuracy.
